hero.title: Ice in Practice
hero.subtitle: A Field Guide to Understanding and Working in the Cryosphere
hero.desc: Ice in Practice is Henry’s first book, a field guide for the people who work where the ice does — polar expedition guides, field operations professionals, and students of the cryosphere. In it, Henry shows that the guides and operators who make the best decisions on glaciers, sea ice, and tidewater termini all share the same habit of mind — and it’s not the one most training programmes teach. He calls this approach Observe → Understand → Decide → Communicate, and it provides a framework that turns a crevasse field or a calving face from a hazard to be feared into a landscape that can be read.
hero.lastLine: And it all starts with learning to read the ice.

intro.quote: The ice is changing faster than the people who work on it can be trained. Ice in Practice is a field guide for reading a cryosphere in transition — for guides, operators, and students whose decisions depend on understanding what the ice is about to do, not what it used to do.
